characters.yaw_prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve. Production directional head animation atlas for an existing cute parrot.
Input image 1 is the existing rig sheet: its TOP-LEFT cell is the identity and neutral detached head. Input image 2 is the original complete character, a style reference. Preserve the SAME character's face proportions, colors, beak anatomy, eye highlights, cheeks and exact illustration style. mint-green rosy-faced lovebird with peach-pink cheeks, large warm brown-black eyes, ivory hooked beak. Soft detailed matte feather shading. No crest.
Create one clean genuinely transparent wide atlas arranged in EXACTLY FIVE EQUAL COLUMNS and THREE EQUAL ROWS, an invisible regular 5 by 3 grid. Fifteen detached heads only, each wholly within its own cell, consistent camera distance and physical cranium size, centered with its neck connection aligned at the SAME bottom-center height in each cell. Generous transparent padding; no body, neck stalk, wings, feet, tail or tuft/crest.
COLUMNS specify true 3D head direction, not sideways movement of a frontal face:
Column 1: turned clearly toward the VIEWER'S LEFT, beak pointing LEFT, approximately 45-degree left three-quarter view, with correct eye occlusion and beak foreshortening.
Column 2: a gentle approximately 20-degree LEFT head turn.
Column 3: the approved neutral forward head, matching the input top-left identity precisely.
Column 4: a gentle approximately 20-degree RIGHT head turn.
Column 5: turned clearly toward the VIEWER'S RIGHT, beak pointing RIGHT, approximately 45-degree right three-quarter view, correct eye occlusion and foreshortening.
ROWS are matched eyelid states of the identical head in that column:
Row 1: relaxed fully open eyes and closed beak.
Row 2: eyelids halfway closed over the SAME eyes, closed beak. Do not shrink the entire eyeballs.
Row 3: eyes gently fully closed, feather-colored lids and small curved closed-eye lines, closed beak.
Within a column, all three heads must have identical silhouette, feather pattern, light, cheek placement, pose and beak position; only eyelids change. Across columns the head must actually turn, retaining the reference identity. Do NOT copy the same fixed face into all columns. Do NOT simply mirror the original lighting. Keep the original light consistent in world space. All viewpoints charming, anatomically coherent and suitable for smooth desktop-pet animation. No labels, numbers, text, grid lines, backgrounds, frames, floor shadows, watermarks or extra items. Preserve fine feather edges with true alpha. Favor accurate identity, strong angle differences and clean consistent rig registration.
characters.pitch_prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve. Production head-pitch and feather-preening head atlas for an existing cute desktop parrot.
Image 1 is the approved detached-parts atlas; its TOP-LEFT cell is the head identity. Image 2 is the complete original character for exact style. mint-green rosy-faced lovebird with peach-pink cheeks, large warm brown-black eyes, ivory hooked beak. Soft detailed matte feather shading. No crest.
Create a genuinely transparent regular atlas of EXACTLY FOUR equal COLUMNS and THREE equal ROWS, twelve detached heads only. Each head is fully inside its cell with generous transparent margin, same physical cranium size, identical original colors, feather texture, face proportions, camera distance and consistent world-space lighting. No bodies, neck stalks, wings, feet, tails, detached crests or extra props.
Column 1: head tipped upward about 20 degrees, eyes and beak visibly looking UP, correct foreshortening.
Column 2: head tipped downward about 25 degrees, eyes and beak visibly looking DOWN toward its chest.
Column 3: a genuine preening head pose, turned LEFT and bent DOWN about 45 degrees toward its own left wing. Beak visibly points diagonally DOWN-LEFT, almost profile; back of cranium comes forward slightly, cute focused body-care expression. This is NOT a front face shifted left: the head must turn anatomically, with appropriate eye occlusion. It will be rigged so the beak tip touches left shoulder/wing feathers.
Column 4: matching preening pose turned RIGHT and bent DOWN toward its own right wing, beak tip points diagonally DOWN-RIGHT, anatomically correct opposite viewpoint with consistent lighting. It will touch right shoulder feathers.
Row 1: fully open relaxed eyes, beak closed.
Row 2: eyes halfway closed, same beak and exact head pose.
Row 3: eyes gently fully closed with natural curved eyelid lines, same beak and exact head pose.
Within each column, duplicate precisely the same head silhouette, cheek location, feather detail and beak position in all three rows; only eyelids change. Between columns show unmistakable upward/downward/preening orientation. Do not add the separately rigged crest/tuft. Keep neck attachment and scale registered to prevent animation jitter. No outlines or texture style changes, no generic owl redesign, no labels, no words, no numbers, no grid, no checkerboard painted into the image, no shadows cast onto a background, no watermark. True transparent alpha around every head.
characters.forward_prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve. Registered forward expression atlas for an existing parrot animation.
Image 1 is a FIVE-COLUMN THREE-ROW directional head atlas. Use ONLY the CENTER HEAD IN ITS TOP ROW (row 1 column 3) as your exact neutral reference. That new forward head must match the adjacent turning views in a continuous animation. mint-green rosy-faced lovebird with peach-pink cheeks, large warm brown-black eyes, ivory hooked beak. Soft detailed matte feather shading. No crest.
Create a genuinely transparent regular THREE-COLUMN THREE-ROW atlas containing nine copies of that EXACT forward head. Same head size, same camera, same upright pose, same face and beak locations, same light, same feather texture and colors, same silhouette, same original world-space lighting. Only eye expression and the specified mouth opening may change.
Read left to right, top to bottom:
Row 1: neutral fully open eyes with closed beak; eyes 75% open with closed beak; eyes 50% open with closed beak.
Row 2: eyes 25% open with closed beak; eyes gently fully closed; happy smiling closed eyes.
Row 3: attentive wide eyes and closed beak; normal open eyes and open beak as if softly chirping, maintaining the same upper beak anatomy; gently concerned brows with normal open eyes and closed beak.
Every head must align perfectly by neck bottom center and physical cranium size. Eyelids cover the original eyeballs without moving or shrinking them. Keep the entire head within its equal grid cell with ample transparent padding. Heads only: no body, neck stalk, feet, wings, tail, tall crest or swept tuft. These tufts remain a separate rig part. No floating symbols, no background, floor shadow, captions, numbers, text, grid lines, borders, watermarks or extra objects. Preserve the new center forward face from input exactly, not another three-quarter angle.
